title: Career roadmap · Professor
summary: An academic pathway combining cognitive science, HCI, neuro-design, human factors and interdisciplinary research with teaching, publications, grants and doctoral supervision.

facts.Timeline assumption: 2026 is treated as Ph.D. Year 1. The roadmap assumes a research-led Ph.D. producing peer-reviewed work alongside teaching experience, conference participation, research collaborations and grant development. Faculty requirements vary by institution and discipline.

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Build a distinctive interdisciplinary research programme rather than remaining broadly defined as an HCI/cognitive-science scholar. Combine publications with grants, doctoral supervision, industry collaborations, research software and measurable real-world impact.

Career progression

Ph.D. Researcher → Postdoctoral/Research Fellow → Assistant Professor
2030–2035: Assistant Professor → Independent Researcher → Research Grant Principal Investigator
2035–2040: Associate Professor → Research Group Lead → Centre/Programme Director
2040–2046: Professor → Research Centre Head → Department Head / Dean / Academic Research Leader
PhD routes
If further research is pursued after this Ph.D., relevant themes include:

The strongest academic profile will combine a clearly defined research niche with sustained publication, grant and supervision activity. A professor in this field can build a laboratory spanning HCI, cognitive science and neuro-design, collaborate with technology and healthcare researchers where appropriate, supervise doctoral researchers and translate findings into human-centred technology. The research agenda should continue evolving toward human–AI interaction, multimodal interfaces, neurotechnology, accessibility and responsible technology while preserving strong experimental methodology.
